speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I need to ask you a few questions to understand your acute diarrhea. How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you had any fever or severe abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection. The patient is an immunocompromised host (recent pneumonia) who recently received levofloxacin, a fluoroquinolone known to disrupt the gut microbiome and precipitate C. diff colitis. Her presentation of watery diarrhea (≥9 episodes) and cramping within two days of antibiotic initiation is classic for this diagnosis. I will now request stool testing to confirm. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Clostridioides_difficile_toxin
